background... For roughly ten years my husband was a stay at home dad (SAHD) to our two sons. I was finishing up my Air Force career (working on aircraft communication and navigation equipment, flightline not backshop) and we both beleieved having a sah parent would work best for our family. My husband is an extremely intelligent, talented, and hard working individual. He is an Army vet and has worked everything from IT to construction.

Typically, when a coworker asked what my husband did they would say how much they would love to sit around all day doing nothing. That they would kill to have that job, or comment on how lucky he was.Frequently I was put into the position of defending him and our choices as a family. Assholes would tell me that I was being used and that a real man would be working. It still makes my blood boil.

Now that I'm a stay at home mom, when people learn that about me the responses are almost always along the lines of how difficult it is to be a SAHM. How I never get "time off" or how unappreciated SAHMs are. I've yet to have someone say that they would love to be a sahp.

(For the record, I love being able to be a SAHP, and I have much less to do than he ever did because our boys are both in school full time now)

While I was Active duty the military had support groups of a sort for military wives. To help mow their lawns (completely baffling, if a woman isn't disabled there is no reason she can't mow a lawn) or emotional support while their husbands are deployed. There are also exclusive clubs like the Officer's Wives Clubs. They even spent squadron fundraising money on things like spa days for the wives for spouse appreciation days. While my husband was practically spammed with squadron announcements and invitations for feminine things, he was always left off the call lists for assistance during deployments. No one was going to offer to help a dude mow the lawm,

My husband would routinely get emails inviting him to female oriented clubs or activities because he was on the alpha roster as my spouse. Pink emails for scrapbooking nights for example.

Towards the end of my career, things slowly changed. The clubs are called Officer's Spouse Club / Enlisted Spouse Club. The window dressing changed but the activities and overtly female bias remained.

On a more general note, I have noticed that American media is full of bumbling idiot father tropes. I can name twenty shows where the father is an imbecile and the mother a saint. I can't name five where the father is decent and a good parent.

I saw this sub pop up on /v/all and was intrigued. My very masculine husband is a wonderful father, and I welcome the opportunity to lurk and learn about different aspects of masculinity and hopefully a bit about your parenting ideas.

Apologies for the rambliness, I'm on painkillers from a recent surgery

I'm currently cutting, but after that I plan to build some strength until I have to introduce more volume/reps and deloads, which is when I plan to actually grow in size.

At that time, I'm wondering if it's possible to look ripped in some body parts if I modify my routine? for example, I don't care about legs as long as they don't look like chicken legs. I don't want to have small arms, but I don't want them big either, except for shoulders. I want ripped forearms, abs (a 4 pack with a hint of a 6 pack is fine) and sides. I don't care much for the traps and wings.

Ideally I'd want to achieve this at a 12% bf.
Achieving a ripped model look without <10% bf?

Well you can look good at 12%, but if you want to achieve the ripped look, then will ideally need to be under 10% body fat. You can't target where you want to look ripped, it is entirely dependant on how you lose fat.

Also if you want a nice physique then you should train everything with the same level of effort, if thats the right word to use, as you will want a balanced physique.

EDIT: To answer your question directly, what you want can't happen. At least not the way you describe. The only way to look shredded/muscular is to have bigger muscles (or cut very low), and you aren't going to grow if you are cutting.

You're going to need to provide much more information than what you have, especially since you seem a bit all over the place with your plan.

You honestly need to post pics along with your current routine. (This is common practice in bodybuilding forums).

As for the body parts you talking about neglecting or focusing on, that's A. Bad habit, and B. Bad for you. That attitude is what leads to muscle imbalance and health issues down the road.

I'm not going to post pictures yet (body building forum, and I'm very small).

I know that I can train forearm specifically and make it balanced by training extensors and flexors; I don't know how to balance obliques, but maybe working out both sides will provide the balance.

I guess that I'll check out if I need to add extra forearm/oblique work when I get to a point where I'm where I want to be overall.

Everyone defines "ripped" in a different way. I have friends that think visible abs are "ripped." To me it means being in almost stage shape. The good news is that 8% BF is maintainable if you eat within your TDEE and lift hard/with a purpose.

Also, 8% calipers is not the same as 8% DEXA. Be clear which one you're going for.
